{"id": "832c8a65-07c2-45ee-8b7a-51d781abbc0d", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_4tgPdrzT42nGW3pUEbvTOw", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"status\":\"SUCCESS\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prov-thru-purchase.html\",\"content\":\"# Purchase a Provisioned Throughput for an Amazon Bedrock model\\n\\nAmazon Bedrock offers two types of Provisioned Throughput - by Tokens and by Model Units. Refer to the following instructions for the type of Provisioned Throughput you wish to to purchase.\\n\\nTo learn more about the differences between the two types of Provisioned Throughput, see Increase model invocation capacity with Provisioned Throughput in Amazon Bedrock.\\n\\n### Provisioned Throughput by Model Units\\n\\nWhen you purchase a Provisioned Throughput by Model Units for a model, you specify the level of commitment for it and the number of model units (MUs) to allot. For MU quotas, see Amazon Bedrock endpoints and quotas in the AWS General Reference.\\nBefore you can purchase a Provisioned Throughput (with commitment or no commitment), you must first visit the AWS support center\\nto request MUs for your account to be distributed between the Provisioned Throughputs. After your request has been granted, you can purchase a Provisioned Throughput.\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nAfter you purchase the Provisioned Throughput, if it's associated with a custom model, you can change the model by specifying one of the following options:\\n\\n* The base model from which the custom model was customized\\n* Another custom model that was customized from the same base model as the custom model\\n\\nYou can only change the associated model for Provisioned Throughputs associated with a custom model.\\n\\nTo learn how to purchase Provisioned Throughput for a model, choose the tab for your preferred method, and then follow the steps:\\n\\n#### Using Console\\n\\n1. Sign in to the AWS Management Console with an IAM identity that has permissions to use the Amazon Bedrock console. Then, open the Amazon Bedrock console at\\n   <https://console.aws.amazon.com/bedrock>.\\n2. Select **Provisioned Throughput** from the left navigation pane.\\n3. In the **Provisioned Throughput** section, choose\\n   **Purchase Provisioned Throughput**.\\n4. For the **Provisioned Throughput details** section, do the following:\\n\\n   1. In the **Provisioned Throughput name** field, enter a name for the Provisioned Throughput.\\n   2. Under **Select model**, select a base model provider or a custom model category. Then select the model for which to provision throughput.\\n\\n      **Note:**\\n\\n      To see the base models for which you can purchase Provisioned Throughput without commitment, see the supported models documentation.\\n\\n      In the AWS GovCloud (US) Region, you can only purchase Provisioned Throughput for custom models with no commitment.\\n   3. (Optional) To associate tags with your Provisioned Throughput, expand the **Tags** section and choose **Add new tag**. For more information, see Tagging Amazon Bedrock resources.\\n5. For **Provisioning mode**, select **By Model Units**\\n6. For the **Commitment term & model units** section, do the following:\\n\\n   1. In the **Select commitment term** section, select the amount of time for which you want to commit to using the Provisioned Throughput.\\n   2. In the **Model units** field, enter the desired number of model units (MUs). If you are provisioning a model with commitment, you must first visit the AWS support center to request an increase in the number of MUs that you can purchase.\\n7. Choose **Purchase Provisioned Throughput**.\\n8. Review the note that appears and acknowledge the commitment duration and price by selecting the checkbox. Then choose **Confirm purchase**.\\n9. The console displays the **Provisioned Throughput** overview page. The **Status** of the Provisioned Throughput in the Provisioned Throughput table becomes **Creating**. When the Provisioned Throughput is finished being created, the **Status** becomes **In service**. If the update fails, the **Status** becomes **Failed**.\\n\\n#### Using API\\n\\nTo purchase a Provisioned Throughput, send a CreateProvisionedModelThroughput request with an Amazon Bedrock control plane endpoint.\\n\\nTo learn more about the contents of the request body and the parameters you need to supply to create a Provisioned Throughput by Model Units, see\\nCreateProvisionedModelThroughput in the\\n*Amazon Bedrock API Reference*.\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nTo see the base models for which you can purchase Provisioned Throughput without commitment, see the supported models documentation.\\n\\nIn the AWS GovCloud (US) Region, you can only purchase Provisioned Throughput for custom models with no commitment.\\n\\nThe response returns a `provisionedModelArn` that you can use as a `modelId` in model inference. To check when the Provisioned Throughput is ready for use, send a GetProvisionedModelThroughput request and check that the status is `InService`. If the update fails, its status will be `Failed`, and the GetProvisionedModelThroughput response will contain a `failureMessage`.\\n\\nSee code examples\",\"total_length\":4781,\"start_index\":0,\"end_index\":4781,\"truncated\":false,\"redirected_url\":null,\"error_code\":null}]}}"}]}], "label": "Read Bedrock Provisioned Throughput purchase docs"}

{"id": "bc8b2731-45b2-4969-a09a-7d39602dc1dc", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "You almost certainly can't end this commitment early. Your realistic options are to use the capacity, get ahead of the renewal, or ask AWS about billing.

**What the docs say** (I checked the Bedrock Provisioned Throughput pages):
- You can't delete a Provisioned Throughput by Model Units with a commitment before the term ends. Yours is `SixMonths` through 2027-03-15, so delete isn't available.
- The docs say a Provisioned Throughput automatically renews at the end of each term with the same configuration. The "cancel auto renew" option is documented only for Provisioned Throughput by Tokens. The page doesn't say how renewal works for a Model Units purchase like yours, so don't assume you can opt out.
- You can only change the associated model if it's a custom model. You can switch to its base model or to another custom model from the same base. If `claude-launch-pt` is a base Claude model, you can't repoint it to something else.

**Your options**
1. **Put the capacity to work.** You've already paid for about 112 more days, roughly 2,700 hours, of 1 model unit (multiply that by your hourly rate for the remaining cost). Anything you move onto the provisioned model ARN costs no extra provisioned fee. Candidates are dev or test traffic, evals or batch jobs, or other workloads that currently use on-demand pricing for the same model. You pay per token on-demand, so shifting it saves money without any new commitment.
2. **Deal with renewal now.** Check `get-provisioned-model-throughput` for any auto-renew field, and in the console see whether "Cancel auto renew" appears for this resource. If you can't turn off renewal, you could be locked into another six months in March. Do this well before 2027-03-15.
3. **Open an AWS Support or account-team case.** Early termination isn't a self-service feature, but a delayed launch is a legitimate business reason to ask. I can't promise a credit or an exception, so treat it as a request. Include the resource name, the purchase date and the usage numbers you gave me.
4. **Use the model-swap path if it applies.** If the underlying model is a custom model, you can change it to a related custom or base model. That helps if you have a different workload to move onto it.

**On your usage data**
- Missing datapoints on 12 of 14 days are normal. CloudWatch emits nothing for days with zero invocations.
- 6 invocations and about 5,000 tokens over 14 days confirms the capacity is essentially idle.
- Check that your launch code or test harness isn't calling the base model ID instead of the provisioned model ARN. If it is, you'd see the same low numbers on the PT ARN while the real traffic goes on-demand.

If you give me the region and account, I can run `get-provisioned-model-throughput` myself. That would show whether it's a custom or base model and whether there's any auto-renew setting. It's a read-only call.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
